focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My brother Tomas and I have been digitizing boxes of family photographs, letters, and recordings.
e002	A local cultural center offered us a small exhibition next spring about migration into the neighborhood.
e003	Tomas wants to accept because a public date would help us finish and the material could mean something beyond our family.
e004	I want the archive organized first.
e005	Right now captions are incomplete, some stories conflict, and I worry the exhibition will turn a complicated family history into a clean public narrative.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The exhibition could create momentum and public value, but it also changes the purpose of the archive from preservation to interpretation.
e007	You may not need to finish the whole archive before exhibiting a carefully bounded selection.
e008	The first question is whether you and Tomas agree on what the exhibition is allowed to claim, especially where accounts conflict.
e009	A date can help with completion while also pressuring you to resolve ambiguity cosmetically.
[Turn 2 USER]
e010	I do not think Tomas wants to resolve it cosmetically.
e011	He is usually the one who includes awkward stories.
e012	I am the person who keeps building the catalog and saying we need better dates and names.
e013	He thinks my standard of organization is a way of postponing anything public until nobody is interested.
e014	That hurts because there is some truth in it.
e015	But when he tells stories confidently, relatives often remember them differently.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e016	Then the difference may be less honesty versus polish and more tolerance for incomplete evidence.
e017	Your cataloging protects traceability; his storytelling keeps the material connected to living attention.
e018	An exhibition could show conflicting memories rather than choose among them, although that approach can become a curatorial device that feels cleverer than the family experience.
e019	It would help to identify which disagreements are enriching and which could make someone feel misrepresented.
[Turn 3 USER]
e020	Our aunt Leena is enthusiastic and has already offered to record narration.
e021	Our cousin Mara does not want a letter from her father displayed, even though Tomas says it explains why that branch of the family left.
e022	I agree with Mara about the letter.
e023	Tomas says one person's discomfort should not control a shared history, but he has not said he would use it without permission.
e024	I catch myself treating his argument as a threat when it may be him thinking aloud.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e025	It is useful to separate the principle he is testing from the action he intends.
e026	Mara's objection is specific and should be treated as real, while the broader question of who can speak for shared material remains unresolved.
e027	You could exclude that letter and still acknowledge the missing part of the story, but doing so may shift the narrative in ways other relatives contest.
e028	Consent decisions do not automatically produce a neutral history; they define what kind of public project you are willing to make.
[Turn 4 USER]
e029	That sounds more abstract than the actual relationship.
e030	Tomas found and protected most of these boxes when our grandmother's apartment was cleared.
e031	He feels he took responsibility while I now act like the archive belongs to a process I control.
e032	I did spend hundreds of hours organizing it, but I joined later.
e033	If I insist on a catalog-first approach, he may hear that his years of care count less because they were not systematic.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e034	The labor histories matter.
e035	Formal organization can accidentally become a claim to authority, just as physical custody and early rescue can become one.
e036	You may need to recognize those contributions explicitly before negotiating the exhibition, not because recognition settles final say but because otherwise each procedural disagreement carries an older argument about ownership.
e037	A shared decision process will feel hollow if either of you believes the other's kind of care is treated as secondary.
[Turn 5 USER]
e038	The cultural center says the exhibition can be small—perhaps twenty items—and they are comfortable showing captions as provisional or including two versions of a story.
e039	They need a commitment in a month to reserve the spring slot.
e040	Tomas sees that flexibility as answering my concern.
e041	I feel relieved and also suspicious of my relief, because twenty items still create a frame.
e042	Whatever we choose becomes “our family” to strangers who will not see the rest.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e043	Any selection will create a frame, including waiting until the catalog is complete.
e044	The center's flexibility reduces pressure to pretend certainty, but it does not eliminate authorship.
e045	You could define the exhibition more narrowly—as twenty objects about how family memory is assembled—rather than as a representative family history.
e046	That may be honest, though it risks making the process the subject when Tomas wants the lives and migration stories to remain central.
[Turn 6 USER]
e047	Yes, he would hate an exhibition mainly about archival uncertainty.
e048	He wants people to meet our relatives as people, not examples in a seminar about memory.
e049	I agree with him.
e050	I also learned that our mother would like to see something public while she can still participate actively.
e051	She is not pressuring us, but that changes the cost of waiting for me.
e052	At the same time, she tends to smooth conflict and may support captions that other relatives dispute.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e053	Your mother's wish adds a meaningful time dimension without making speed automatically correct.
e054	Her participation could bring warmth and knowledge, while her preference for harmony is one perspective among several.
e055	The exhibition might be designed around a limited period or theme where the evidence and permissions are stronger, leaving contested material in the archive for later work.
e056	But selecting the least contested material could also produce exactly the smooth family story you are trying to avoid.
[Turn 7 USER]
e057	I am leaning toward accepting the slot, choosing a narrow theme about the family's first ten years in the neighborhood, and limiting the exhibition to material that Tomas and I both support displaying.
e058	We would invite relatives to comment on draft captions and preserve disagreements where they matter, but not give everyone veto over the whole exhibition.
e059	I have not decided what “both support” means if Tomas thinks a disputed object is essential and I think the dispute itself makes it unsuitable.
e060	I also worry a one-month commitment will make that unresolved rule feel settled.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e061	The direction is narrower and more participatory, but the decision rule is still the heart of it.
e062	Requiring both of you to support every object protects the partnership and can also let one person quietly block the story.
e063	Allowing exceptions for “essential” material simply moves the disagreement into defining essential.
e064	You may be able to commit to the slot while telling the center that final object selection depends on a process you have not completed.
e065	That preserves the opportunity, though it also creates pressure and does not guarantee you and Tomas will reach a set you can both stand behind.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.
